title: PJM Interim Resource Adequacy Service & Large Load Registry — FERC 205(d) effective date (docket ER26-3515)
source: EST: govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-19/html/2026-16927.htm (Combined Notice of Filings #1, fetched direct 2026-09-15) — the entry reads verbatim 'PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.', '205(d) Rate Filing: Proposal to Establish Interim Resource Adequacy Service & a Large Load Registry', filed 8/13/26, accession 20260813-5118, EFFECTIVE DATE 10/12/2026, comments due 5 p.m. ET 9/3/26. Corroborated on the same filing date and the same requested deadline by powermag.com/pjm-widens-response-to-data-center-load-as-capacity-shortfalls-deepen/ (published 2026-08-20, fetched 2026-09-15): IRAS filed 2026-08-13 in ER26-3515-000, 'PJM also urged FERC to approve the rule changes by Oct. 12', with the service itself taking effect 2027-06-01 for the 2027/2028 delivery year. Filed estimate on the same two counts the proposing event records: this calendar's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a Federal Register notice of a pending 205(d) filing (no FERC: prefix exists), and no FERC order in ER26-3515 was found on any search run 2026-09-15 — recorded as an ABSENCE, since elibrary.ferc.gov serves no document list to a plain fetcher (re-probed 2026-09-15: HTTP 200 returning an empty Angular shell)
notes: DISCOVERED during the pjm-reliability-backstop-procurement-2026-09-30 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-15). Why it earns a row, and the correction it carries: the proposing event's initial research (2026-09-08) treated PJM's 2026-07-31 filing in ER26-3380 as carrying BOTH the Reliability Backstop Procurement and the Interim Resource Adequacy Service. It does not. IRAS plus a Large Load Registry is its own separate 205(d) docket, ER26-3515-000, filed two weeks later on 2026-08-13 with its own requested effective date of 2026-10-12 — thirteen days after ER26-3380's 2026-09-29 date. That split matters to the proposing event's stance because the organized protest fire is aimed substantially at THIS docket, not at the RBP: the Electric Power Supply Association protested the IRAS proposal (epsa.org/filings/epsa-protests-pjm-interim-resource-adequacy-service-proposal/, search-relayed — the page served no body to a fetcher on 2026-09-15), and PJM's own Independent Market Monitor filed a protest in ER26-3515 dated 2026-09-03 (monitoringanalytics.com/filings/2026/IMM_Protest_Docket_No_ER26-3515_20260903.pdf, fetched 2026-09-15 but its text layer would not parse — recorded in the proposing ledger's probe-ref.blocked, so the docket and date are read from the file name and the search-relayed summary, not from the document body). Impact medium and symbols empty on the proposing ledger's own grounds: no tracked name is an IPP, and the exposed names (VST, CEG, TLN, NRG) live in docs/research/ai-energy-constraint.md rather than on the tracked roster. Estimate throughout — a requested effective date on a protested filing licenses no date-keyed entry, and like its sibling it turns on the FPA section 205(d) default that a filing FERC does not reject, suspend or set for hearing simply takes effect.
